title: Former world champion Joseph Parker cleared to return after testing positive for cocaine
content:
Former world heavyweight champion Joseph Parker has had his provisional suspension for testing positive for cocaine lifted.

The New Zealander is cleared to compete again unless UK Anti-Doping (UKAD) re-open the investigation.

Parker, 34, provided a sample to the Voluntary Anti-Doping Association (Vada) on October 25 — the same day he lost to British fighter Fabio Wardley by 11th-round stoppage — which had an adverse analytical finding for the recreational drug.

Parker insisted the result “came as a real surprise” to him and said he was “confident the investigation will clear my name”.

Because the substance is banned “in competition” by the World Anti-Doping Agency and the bout took place in London under the jurisdiction of the British Boxing Board of Control (BBBoC), it meant UKAD would investigate the matter despite not being the body which the failed test was given to.

Parker was placed under a provisional suspension pending the investigation but he has confirmed that has now been lifted.

“I’m pleased to confirm my provisional suspension is lifted and I’ll be back in the ring soon,” Parker said in a statement.

“I’ve been advised to say no more for now while details are finalised. Thank you to all my supporters.”

The BBBoC confirmed to The Athletic that Parker’s provisional suspension has been lifted but added it “cannot make any further comment at this stage”.

The Athletic also contacted UKAD but they have yet to respond.

Parker is a former WBO champion and has four defeats and 36 wins in his 40 professional fights.
